Altered Endothelin-1 levels may be involved in the pathogenesis of rebound hypertension and hypotension during hemodialysis. This suggests that endothelin-1 plays a role in the hemodynamic changes experienced by patients undergoing hemodialysis, which can include fluctuations in blood pressure.

In detail, this means that elevated or decreased levels of endothelin-1 could contribute to the development of complications such as rebound hypertension and hypotension, which are common issues during hemodialysis. These complications can be life-threatening if left unmanaged, highlighting the importance of monitoring endothelin-1 levels in patients undergoing this treatment.

While more research is needed to fully understand the role of endothelin-1 in hemodialysis-induced hemodynamic changes, these findings provide a promising area for investigation and potential therapeutic target for improving patient outcomes.
